newsitem.title: FRANCE: Historic Algerian opponent raps military rule.
newsitem.headline: Historic Algerian opponent raps military rule.

text.p: A leader of Algeria's secular political opposition, Hocine Ait Ahmed, accused the country's military rulers in an interview published on Friday of trying to run the country "like a barracks".

Ait Ahmed, 70, who heads the Socialist Forces Front (FFS), told the French daily Le Monde that the international community was worsening civil strife in Algeria through indifference, effectively giving a blank cheque to President Liamine Zeroual.

"The support of part of the international community for the regime is aggravating the situation. It is revolting when you think that two bombs on a market in Sarajevo caused a Western media storm about Bosnia, but in today's Algeria the wave of attacks going on provokes not the slightest reaction," he said.
"A civil war is going on two hours' flight from Paris and nobody is lifting a finger. This silence of the international community is a blank cheque for the regime of General Zeroual."
Ait Ahmed said Zeroual and his military colleagues had decided to manage the country through violence, using the Islamic fundamentalist "threat" as a pretext while barring any real democratisation.
"The rulers want to reduce everything to an equation "army versus fundamentalism'," he said.
At least 50,000 people have been killed since the military intervened five years ago to halt a general election in which the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a big lead on the first ballot.
"Without the political, diplomatic, logistic and financial support of Paris, the Algerian regime would not have been capable of conducting this war which is now in its sixth year," Ait Ahmed said.

"Without this international complicity, the regime would have been forced to negotiate with representative political forces. In the FFS' talks both with the European Union and the United States, we have often been told that France will not accept any external political initiative on Algeria," he said.
"We have the feeling that France's Algerian policy is a hostage to the Algerian lobby," Ait Ahmed added.
He called on the French parliament and media to open a debate on the real causes and solutions to the crisis.
